subject: Subprocessor roster + crypto/KMS access questions for SOC2 review
messages:
From: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@neurolytix.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytix.com
Date: 2027-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor roster + crypto/KMS access questions for SOC2 review

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off the SOC2 evidence collection for Neurolytix's procurement review and need a few items clarified for your subprocessor and crypto posture. Could you provide the following by EOD Tuesday: 

- The current subprocessor roster (including role: hosting, telemetry, key escrow, analytics) and which ones are authorized to handle any encrypted customer data or key material.
- For any KMS/key-escrow providers: do they hold wrapped keys only, or do they have the ability to unwrap/see plaintext?
- A diagram or short description of the KMS keyflow (where keys originate, who can rotate, where HSMs are located i.e. region/onshore/offshore).
- Evidence that any escrow partner has a recent SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) audit, or a plan to provide one.

If helpful, procurement is copied for contract references. Thank you — this helps close a dependency blocking our security acceptance.

Regards,
Anna Lewis
Sr. Security Program Manager | Neurolytix
anna.lewis@neurolytix.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

(Attachment expectation: subprocessor roster CSV, any SOC2 artifacts)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@neurolytix.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytix.com, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + crypto/KMS access questions for SOC2 review

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Please find the initial artifacts attached and answers inline. Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_list.csv; kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx; kms-keyflow-diagram.pdf.

Short answers up front:
- Subprocessor roster attached with role column populated. We mark KMS/escrow providers explicitly (CloudVault and KeyBath).
- CloudVault is used as an escrow partner for long-term backup of wrapping keys; they hold wrapped keys only (they do NOT have unwrap/cleartext privileges).
- Our runtime uses ephemeral keys for model serving; those are generated by Redwood's KMS and only the serving runtime has transient unwrapped access in memory. Persistent plaintext is not stored by any subprocessor.
- CloudVault maintains HSM-backed key wrapping in us-east-1; KeyBath (backup) has HSM in eu-west-1.

Notes and clarifications:
- "Ability to unwrap" is managed by access control in our KMS (RBAC + key policies). Only a small set of operator service accounts can request unwrap operations and every request is logged and audited.
- KV cache: the inference runtime uses an encrypted KV cache (at-rest encrypted with customer-derived keys). KV caches are not stored by CloudVault.

If you need our auditor contact or a redacted SOC2 report from CloudVault, we can provide a redacted copy. We can also schedule a technical call with Logan to run through the keyflow diagram and audit controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Accept attached roster + matrix for initial review.
2) We'll upload a redacted CloudVault SOC2 next business day (pending their permission).
3) Tech call (30m) if you want to walk through keyflow.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Supplier Security Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
(650) 555-0210

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_list.csv (CSV) | kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx (XLSX) | kms-keyflow-diagram.pdf (PDF)

From: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@neurolytix.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytix.com
Date: 2027-07-12T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + crypto/KMS access questions for SOC2 review

Thanks Soojin — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the matrix:

On Tue, Jul 12, 2027 at 11:00 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> CloudVault is used as an escrow partner for long-term backup of wrapping keys; they hold wrapped keys only (they do NOT have unwrap/cleartext privileges).

Can you confirm/answer:
1) Do you have a signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) or subprocessor agreement with CloudVault that explicitly prohibits unwrapping/cleartext access? If yes, please attach the DPA clause reference or redacted contract excerpt.
2) Can CloudVault provide their most recent SOC2 Type II report or AICPA letter? If they require an NDA, let us know and we'll sign.
3) For the ephemeral keys used in serving (you mentioned runtime has transient unwrapped access): what is the maximum TTL for those keys and who (which Redwood roles/service accounts) can invoke unwrap?
4) Any offshore processing for inference or backups? The row for KeyBath looks like eu-west-1 but we want explicit confirmation that no PII/plaintext crosses outside the US for Neurolytix customer data.

Procurement: we need the DPA excerpt and SOC2 evidence to clear vendor risk.

Thanks — can you try to get the redacted SOC2 + contract excerpt before EOD Wednesday? If you need an NDA, we can route it quickly.

Regards,
Anna

(Attachment: none)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@neurolytix.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + crypto/KMS access questions for SOC2 review

Hi Anna — looping in some technical detail to answer your questions. Attachments: cloudvault-soc2-report-redacted.pdf; kms-escrow-config-snippet.txt.

1) DPA / contract: Yes — we have a DPA and a subprocessor agreement with CloudVault that includes explicit language limiting them to key-wrapping/wrapped-key storage and forbids plaintext access. I'll ask legal to provide a redacted excerpt; for speed we've attached a config snippet showing key-wrap-only policy identifiers (see kms-escrow-config-snippet.txt).

2) SOC2 evidence: CloudVault gave us a redacted SOC2 Type II that covers key management operations; attached is the redacted summary they permit us to share. If Neurolytix needs the full report under an NDA, we'll coordinate that with CloudVault.

3) Ephemeral key TTL / unwrap rights: Ephemeral keys for serving are time-limited to a maximum TTL of 15 minutes by default (configurable per-customer down to 1 minute). Unwrap operations can be executed only by the serving runtime principal (service account: infra/runtime-serve) and the key-rotation operator role (ops/key-rotate). All unwrap calls generate an audit entry and require a validated signed request.

4) Offshore processing: KeyBath (eu-west-1) is used strictly for geo-redundant wrapped-key backup; they do not process ciphertext-to-plaintext operations for Neurolytix. No Neurolytix plaintext is exported to eu-west-1. Production inference serving for Neurolytix (by contract) is routed through us-east-1 only.

If helpful, we can do a short technical onboarding call (20-30m) to walk the keyflow diagram and the SOC2 artifacts. Please confirm if NDA is required to receive the full CloudVault report and we'll expedite.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
(650) 555-0177
